newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir commander complains of health problem.
newsitem.headline: Mir commander complains of health problem.

text.p: Vasily Tsibliyev, the cosmonaut preparing to carry out risky repairs to the Mir space station, told Mission Control on Monday he had developed a health problem after Mir collided with a cargo craft on June 25.

Reporters could not make out his description of the problem during a television link-up because of poor sound quality. But they heard a doctor advising Tsibliyev, the station commander: "The main thing is not to worry. I cannot recommend any medicine for you. Try to rest as much as possible."
There was no immediate official comment. Tsibliyev referred to the problem during an unusually long, 60-minute, television linkup organised with the help of U.S. communication stations.
"I developed this several days after June 25. It came as a surprise," he said during the exchange, part of which was unintelligable due to crackles on the link.
On that day a Progress cargo ship crashed into Mir during a redocking exercise conducted by Tsibliyev manually. The Spektr scientific module attached to Mir was holed.

Tsibliyev asked the doctor whether he could take some medicine, but the doctor advised him against it before he and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin enter Spektr for repair works. The risky and complex sortie is planned later this week.
